what_ptolemy_says: I.22 (Loeb pp.109-111): the beginnings of the signs are to be reckoned "from the equinoxes and solstices", i.e. the tropical zodiac.
what_the_app_does: The signs are read as the real IAU constellations on the ecliptic, at their true widths, as in Lilly mode (user decision). This is a deliberate departure from Ptolemy.

what_ptolemy_says: III.10 (Loeb p.273): the first place runs from 5° above the horizon through the 25° that follow; the others are the twelfth parts in sextile, quartile, trine and opposition to it.
what_the_app_does: Constellation places (user decision): place 1 is the whole IAU constellation that holds the point 5° above the Ascendant; places 2-12 are the constellations that follow. Ophiuchus is joined to Scorpius's place, so there are twelve. Places are therefore unequal.

what_ptolemy_says: The terms are given in degrees of a 30° sign (I.21).
what_the_app_does: Each constellation is rescaled to 30 degrees, so a planet halfway through a constellation is at 15°.

what_ptolemy_says: I.21 (Loeb p.107) gives the "Terms according to Ptolemy". They differ from the table in Lilly (p.104) in eight signs.
what_the_app_does: Ptolemy mode uses the I.21 table. In Libra the LacusCurtius transcription repeats ♄ in the last term; the app reads ♂ 6, the only planet missing from that row.

what_ptolemy_says: Ptolemy ranks the testimonies (I.23, I.24, III.10) but gives no numbers.
what_the_app_does: The net score uses app weights on Lilly's scale (house +5, exaltation +4, triangle +3, terms +2 ...). They are listed in data/ptolemy_testimonies.csv and data/ptolemy_places.csv and can be edited.

what_ptolemy_says: III.13 (Loeb pp.339-341): a planet with "a dignified position with reference to the universe and the angles", or "the opposite".
what_the_app_does: Honourable = net score above zero (dignities + place + phase); the opposite = below zero; zero = neither, read with the honourable text.

what_ptolemy_says: Ptolemy gives no orbs for aspects (III.10 mentions rays of Jupiter up to 12° and Venus up to 8° in prorogation only).
what_the_app_does: Aspects use the medieval moieties of orbs (Lilly p.107), the same as Lilly mode.

what_ptolemy_says: III.2-III.3: the ruler is the planet related to the place by most of the five ways: trine, house, exaltation, term, and phase or aspect.
what_the_app_does: Counts the five ways for the Ascendant degree; "phase or aspect" = an aspect to the degree within the planet's moiety. Ties go to the planet in the place of greater authority (III.10), then the one of the sect, then the higher net score.

what_ptolemy_says: III.13: the planet that dominates Mercury and the Moon governs the soul.
what_the_app_does: Counts the five ways for Mercury's and the Moon's degrees together; the planet with most is named. Its III.13 passage is the one shown first.

what_ptolemy_says: I.23 (Loeb p.111): a planet keeps to the Sun or Moon the aspect its house has to their houses.
what_the_app_does: Counted when the planet stands at that angle from the Sun (east of it) or the Moon (west of it) within 3°.

what_ptolemy_says: III.13 (Loeb pp.335-337): "Precessions and settings make them easily changed, unstable, weak".
what_the_app_does: A planet within 15° of the Sun counts as setting under the rays.

what_ptolemy_says: III.13 (Loeb p.361): the Moon contributes by her phase, her nodes and her limits of latitude.
what_the_app_does: The Moon's reading quotes the waxing or the waning clause by her actual phase, and adds the clause on the nodes when she is within 6° of a node.

what_ptolemy_says: III.13 speaks of "solstitial" signs; I.11 separates solstitial (Cancer, Capricorn) from equinoctial (Aries, Libra).
what_the_app_does: For III.13 the four turning signs are taken together.

what_ptolemy_says: Not one of Ptolemy's twelve signs.
what_the_app_does: A planet there has no familiarity (-1); if it holds the point 5° above the Ascendant, the horoscope has no ruler.

what_ptolemy_says: The Tetrabiblos has no rules for questions (horary), for choosing times (elections), or for planetary hours.
what_the_app_does: The Forecast in Ptolemy mode reads the moment as a nativity is read (sect, lights, angles, rulers, Lot of Fortune). The Auspicious dates page and the four undertakings keep Lilly's election rules in both modes (user decision), and say so.

what_ptolemy_says: III.10, IV.2: the same reckoning by day and by night.
what_the_app_does: The engine already computes it so (Ascendant + Moon - Sun).
Quotations are from F. E. Robbins's Loeb translation (1940), in the public domain in the United States (copyright not renewed), as transcribed on LacusCurtius.
